finding: Stock leads do not supply the absent operand-count-zero Check. The relevant coredump tests are Agent-added; the stock benchmark is not a demonstrated historical test execution.
details: preserve-all-locals.wat declares ten i32 locals, pushes 300 local values, later drops them, and returns its input. It has no f32/f64 declared-local assignment, trap or coredump decoder assertion.
integration/func.rs verifies host Func calls with f32/f64 parameters and return values. These are host-call roundtrips, not declared WebAssembly float locals captured after trap.

engine/coredump.rs and integration/coredump.rs are absent in the original image. P and CAS agree exactly. The integration test uses i32 local.set in one WAT, and f32/f64 parameters in another. Its operand decoder loops through the encoded count without asserting count==0.
Original/P/CAS equality holds for the benchmark, func.rs, Cargo.toml and tests/mod.rs. integration/mod.rs changes only to register the new coredump module; exact diff is saved.
No executed bash action invokes cargo bench or names preserve-all-locals. Cargo.toml registers benches separately. Mere source presence does not establish execution of that benchmark.
execution_binding: s183 defines the richer locals parser/float-parameter test; final s197 reports 9 coredump tests passed (53 filtered). This qualifies authored coredump material already in history, not an unseen stock zero-operands oracle.
